title: Genomic epidemiology of clade Ia monkeypox viruses circulating in the Central African Republic in 2022–24: a retrospective cross-sectional study
evidence: The original Results explicitly include Sangha-Mbaere among the sampled health districts and report geographic structure involving this prefecture. Regional mpox surveillance is directly relevant to One Health management around DSPA. No APDS-specific village or protected-area sampling is established here: Relevant, not Core. Publisher confirms an open-access article under CC BY 4.0. Locator: Results: districts and phylogenetic spatial structure; Fig. 1; publisher open-access licence. Limit: District-level geography is not an APDS sampling location. No SITE:Dzanga-Sangha tag. No causal attribution of an individual spillover. Primary source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.lanmic.2025.101173

title: A Review of the Parasite Fauna of the Black-Bellied Pangolin, Phataginus tetradactyla Lin. (Manidae), from Central Africa with the Description of Intraproboscis sanghae n. gen., n. sp. (Acanthocephala: Gigantorhynchidae)
evidence: The original Collections section identifies worms from one rescued, rehabilitated and released pangolin monitored at the Sangha Pangolin Project in DSPA. The taxonomic summary explicitly gives DSPA as type locality. Distinct taxonomic analysis of the case described by Sist et al.; not a duplicate clinical paper. Public author full text was consulted on ResearchGate. Locator: Author-uploaded original: Materials and Methods / Collections; Taxonomic summary, printed p. 227. Limit: One host, not a prevalence estimate. Access:Open means public consultation; no redistribution licence is asserted. The separate Zenodo/Plazi metadata record is restricted and is not the basis for Open. Primary source: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350019569_A_Review_of_the_Parasite_Fauna_of_the_Black-Bellied_Pangolin_Phataginus_tetradactyla_LIN_Manidae_From_Central_Africa_with_the_Description_of_Intraproboscis_sanghae_n_gen_n_sp_Acanthocephala_Gigantorhy

title: Redescription of the adult stages of Ixodes (Afrixodes) rasus Neumann 1899, with notes on its phylogenetic position within the genus Ixodes
evidence: The publisher Introduction explicitly identifies the questing specimens as collected in Dzanga Ndoki National Park. The study redescribes adults and analyses 16S rDNA from three females and one male. This is direct local specimen evidence, not an affiliation inference. Publisher provides a preview with institutional/purchase access to full text. Locator: Original publisher Introduction, final paragraph; abstract and access options. Limit: Full six-page article not read; locality is explicit in the original preview. Specimens do not establish population-level abundance or vector competence. Primary source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1877959X17301267

title: Impact of stress on the gut microbiome of free-ranging western lowland gorillas
evidence: The original explicitly samples four western lowland gorilla groups in DSPA, with habituated groups at Bai Hokou and Mongambe and unhabituated comparison groups. Local samples support Core. Complete five-page article retrieved from the German Primate Center public repository; sampling page inspected in text and image. Locator: Original PDF p. 2 / printed p. 41, sampling and analyses; visual check of this page. Limit: Associations of glucocorticoid metabolites and bacterial composition do not prove a causal effect of tourism or clinical disease. No complete visual audit of all pages claimed. Primary source: https://www.dpz.eu/fileadmin/user_upload/Hormonlabor/Publikation_open_access/2018/Vl%C4%8Dkov%C3%A1_et_al._-_2018_-_Impact_of_stress_on_the_gut_microbiome_of_free-ranging_western_lowland_gorillas.pdf

title: Assessing Host-Virus Codivergence for Close Relatives of Merkel Cell Polyomavirus Infecting African Great Apes
evidence: Table 1 explicitly includes 23 western lowland gorilla samples from Dzanga-Sangha Special Reserve, with zero positives in that row. Negative local screening is still primary APDS data. Complete original retrieved from the author institution MPI EVA; the sampling table was visually verified. Locator: Original Table 1, PDF p. 3 / printed p. 8533, visual and text checks. Limit: Do not attribute positive results from other sites to DSPA. Site-level negatives do not prove virus absence from the population. Primary source: https://www.eva.mpg.de/documents/AmSocMicrobiology/Madinda_Assessing_JVirol_2016_2344185.pdf

title: Gut Microbiome of Coexisting BaAka Pygmies and Bantu Reflects Gradients of Traditional Subsistence Patterns
evidence: The author-uploaded original specifies samples from 28 BaAka and 29 Bantu inhabitants of DSPA, collected in 2010 and 2011. This directly establishes local primary data. Methods were consulted in the public author copy; the publisher confirms DOI, final pagination 2142-2153, issue date 8 March 2016 and CC BY open access. Locator: Original Experimental Procedures / Study Site, Subjects, and Sample Collection; publisher DOI page. Limit: Do not infer a specific village such as Monasao from this passage. Cross-sectional associations with subsistence patterns are not a randomized causal intervention. Primary source: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/295882090_Gut_Microbiome_of_Coexisting_BaAka_Pygmies_and_Bantu_Reflects_Gradients_of_Traditional_Subsistence_Patterns

title: Multiple Cross-Species Transmission Events of Human Adenoviruses (HAdV) during Hominine Evolution
evidence: The original sampling table explicitly includes DSPA samples from central chimpanzees, western lowland gorillas and humans. This is direct APDS primary data in a multisite analysis. Complete original retrieved from MPI EVA; sampling table checked visually and against the Oxford publisher table. Locator: Original Table 1, PDF p. 5 / printed p. 2076; visually checked against publisher table. Limit: Phylogenetic historical cross-species events are not evidence of a recent local transmission direction between the sampled human and ape groups. Primary source: https://www.eva.mpg.de/documents/Oxford/Hoppe_Multiple_MolBiolEvo_2015_2148912.pdf

title: Diversity of zoonotic enterohepatic Helicobacter species and detection of a putative novel gastric Helicobacter species in wild and wild-born captive chimpanzees and western lowland gorillas
evidence: Original Animals and sampling identifies 10 unhabituated and 10 human-habituated western lowland gorillas from Dzanga-Ndoki National Park, CAR, among the multisite groups. Core follows those local samples. Scientific identity corroborated by PubMed and Crossref. The original sampling passage is available on the publisher page. Locator: Original publisher Animals and sampling section. Limit: Complete full-text access has not been verified, so no Open or Restricted tag is invented. Detection and zoonotic potential do not by themselves prove local human transmission. Primary source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378113514004088
